name: merman

attributes.attribute: the male form of the sea fairy in Irish and Scottish tales
rarely handsome, with pig-like eyes and a red nose
enjoyed brandy from wrecked ships and raw fish
a captured one was kept for a time as the Wild Man of Oxford

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The mermaid has a male counterpart, the merman. Irish and Scottish folk lore knew him as Dinny-Mara or Dooinney Marrey. The sea fairies of Celtic story were usually female, but the merman appears now and then. Unlike the fair mermaid, the merman was rarely handsome. He had pig-like eyes and a red nose. His red nose came from living on brandy drawn from wrecked ships. His breath smelled of the fish he ate from the sea. The English chronicler said a merman was taken alive during the reign of King John. His keepers named him the Wild Man of Oxford. He did not live long in captivity.
objective: Document the merman, the male form of the Celtic sea fairy.
